message: The page has no <meta name="viewport">. On a narrow screen the browser lays the page out in a wider virtual viewport and shrinks it, so a responsive app looks like a small desktop page.
fix: Add <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> to the <head>.

message: Neither the page (<meta name="theme-color">) nor the manifest (theme_color) sets a theme color, so the browser draws its own frame around the app.
fix: Add <meta name="theme-color" content="#..."> and "theme_color" in the manifest.
source_section: Meta names defined in the HTML specification

message: The manifest has no id, so the identity of the app is its start_url. If start_url changes later, the browser sees a different app and the installed one is not updated.
fix: Add "id", for example "/" or "/recipes/", and keep it as it is for the life of the app.

message: start_url (/index.html) is not within scope (/recipes/), so the scope is ignored and the browser uses the folder of start_url instead.
fix: Make scope a path that start_url begins with, for example the folder of start_url.

message: The display mode is "browser", which is not one of fullscreen, standalone, minimal-ui or window-controls-overlay, the modes that the install criteria accept.
source_page: What does it take to be installable?

message: No icon has the purpose "maskable". An icon without it can be cropped or shown on a plain background by the system, and the specification says an icon is only to be used for its stated purpose.
fix: Add a 512x512 icon with "purpose": "maskable", with the artwork inside the safe zone.

message: The icon icons/icon-256.svg names /icons/icon-256.svg, and no such file is in the folder. A browser cannot use an icon that it cannot fetch (this conclusion is the tool's own).
fix: Add the image at that path, or correct src.

message: The icon icons/icon-256.svg has no sizes, so the browser cannot choose it by size.
fix: Add "sizes", for example "192x192", the exact size of the image.

message: The icon icons/icon-256.svg has no type, so the browser infers the image type from the file extension.

The manifest member icons[2].src is http://recipebox.example/icons/icon-512.svg, an address that is served over http. A service worker needs a secure context, and the install criteria name HTTPS, so the app cannot be installed or work offline from there.
fix: Serve the app and every address it names over https. http is allowed only for localhost and the loopback addresses, for development.

message: register() asks for the scope /, but the worker is at /js/sw.js, so the widest scope it can have is /js/. The registration fails unless the server sends a Service-Worker-Allowed header for the worker file; the tool does not see headers.
fix: Move the worker to /, or narrow the scope, or send Service-Worker-Allowed with the worker.

message: The worker caches /img/logo.png, and no such file is in the folder. The list is relative to the worker file, and the install fails if one file in it cannot be fetched, so the app gets no offline copy (this conclusion about the file is the tool's own).
fix: Remove the file from the list, or add the file, or correct the path.

message: The worker caches /offline.html, and no such file is in the folder. The list is relative to the worker file, and the install fails if one file in it cannot be fetched, so the app gets no offline copy (this conclusion about the file is the tool's own).
fix: Remove the file from the list, or add the file, or correct the path.

message: The worker calls skipWaiting(), so a new version takes over at once, while pages that the old version controls are still open. Those pages and the new worker can disagree about the files and the cache (this conclusion is the tool's own).
fix: Keep it only if the new worker works with the pages of the old version, or ask the user to reload.

message: The cache is named "recipe-box", with no version in the name, and the worker has no activate handler that deletes old caches. When the files change, the old copies stay in the browser until something clears them (this conclusion is the tool's own).
fix: Put a version in the cache name (for example "app-v2") and, in the activate handler, delete the caches whose names are not the current one.
source_section: Install and activate: populating your cache

message: The fetch handler has no fallback for a request that cannot be answered: no catch that returns a cached page or a Response, and no cached offline page matched by a fixed address. When the network is gone and a page is not in the cache, the browser shows its own error page.
fix: Cache an offline page when the worker installs, and return it from a catch (caches.match("/offline.html")) when a navigation fails.

message: The worker puts responses into a cache and never looks at the request method. A cache accepts only GET requests, so a POST or another method makes put() fail with a TypeError (this conclusion about your code is the tool's own).
fix: Cache only when event.request.method === "GET", and let other requests go to the network.
